title: Present tense, common -re and 3rd group verbs: prendre, mettre, venir, partir
goal: By the end of this lesson you can conjugate prendre, mettre, venir and partir (plus sortir and dormir) in the present and use them in everyday sentences about transport, food, clothes and coming and going.

body: *Prendre* (to take) is used for transport, food and drinks: *prendre le métro*, *prendre un café*. Watch the plural: the d disappears and *ils prennent* has a double n.
*Mettre* (to put, to put on) is used for objects and clothes: *Je mets mon manteau.* One t in the singular, two t's in the plural.
Verbs built on them follow the same pattern: *apprendre* (to learn), *comprendre* (to understand), *promettre* (to promise), *permettre* (to allow).
learn.tip: Il prend (d), il met (t): the singular keeps the last letter of the stem.

body: *Venir* (to come) changes its vowel: *je viens* but *nous venons*, and *ils viennent* with a double n. *Revenir* (to come back) and *devenir* (to become) work the same way.
*Venir de* + place = to come from: *Je viens de Toronto.* *Venir de* + infinitive = to have just done something: *Je viens de manger.* (I just ate.)
learn.tip: Je viens de… has two meanings: 'I'm from' (+ place) and 'I just' (+ verb).

body: These -ir verbs do NOT take *-iss-*. In the singular, drop the last consonant of the stem: *partir → je pars*, *sortir → je sors*, *dormir → je dors*. In the plural, keep it: *nous partons*, *ils sortent*, *vous dormez*.
*Partir* = to leave (a place): *Je pars à huit heures.* *Sortir* = to go out: *On sort ce soir.* *Dormir* = to sleep.

learn.h: Quebec: prendre une marche and other calques
body: In Quebec, you'll hear *prendre une marche* (take a walk) everywhere. It's a calque of English; the standard form is *faire une promenade* or *aller marcher*, which Quebecers also say.
Also common: *Viens-t'en!* (Come on! Come here!), and in speech *j'pars*, *y viennent* (ils viennent), *a sort* (elle sort).

examples.en: I take the metro every morning.

examples.en: Where do you put the keys?
My friends are coming on Saturday.

examples.en: The train leaves in five minutes.

quebec.intro: Quebec French borrows the shape of some English expressions: 'prendre une marche' (take a walk) is the classic. It's normal in conversation; in formal writing use 'faire une promenade'.

items.en: I'm going to take a walk.
items.note: prendre une marche: everyday Quebec, a calque of English
j'm'en vas = je m'en vais (I'm off), casual
à soir = ce soir in Quebec speech

items.en: She's going out with her friends.

items.note: another English calque, very common in Quebec speech

dialogue.fr: Je prends une marche après le souper. Tu viens?
dialogue.en: I'm taking a walk after supper. Are you coming?

dialogue.fr: Oui, mais je viens de manger. Deux minutes!
dialogue.en: Yes, but I just ate. Two minutes!

dialogue.fr: Mets ton manteau, il fait froid.
dialogue.en: Put your coat on, it's cold.

dialogue.fr: Je mets aussi ma tuque. Les enfants viennent?
dialogue.en: I'm putting my toque on too. Are the kids coming?

questions.q: Why does B need two minutes?
What does B put on besides the coat?

speak.prompt: Say how you get to work or school and when you leave home.
speak.model: Je pars à sept heures et demie. Je prends l'autobus, puis le métro.

speak.prompt: Say where you come from, and something you have just done.
speak.model: Je viens de Toronto. Je viens de finir mon café.

speak.prompt: Suggest a walk after supper, the standard way and the Quebec way.
speak.model: On fait une promenade après le souper? / On prend une marche après le souper?

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about a typical morning: when you leave, what you take, what you put on, who comes with you.
write.model: Le matin, je prends un café et des rôties. Je mets mon manteau et mes bottes. Je pars à huit heures. Je prends l'autobus avec ma voisine. Elle vient de Sherbrooke. Le soir, je reviens à six heures.

quiz.why: nous prenons: no d, one n.

quiz.q: Which verb follows the prendre pattern?
quiz.why: Comprendre and apprendre conjugate like prendre; rendre, vendre and attendre are regular -re verbs.
